incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Laws of Gibraltar, Cap. 65), ss. 3–21 (mode of incorporation), ss. 22–30 (memorandum and articles), ss. 88–112 (directors and company secretary), ss. 115–118 (registered office); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2019; Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010, s. 8 and Eighth Schedule (exemption / non-resident status).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, a directorate of the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), Europort, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Private Company Limited by Shares (Form 1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and registered-office consent (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The company, formed under the Cayman-style exempted template, ordinarily adopts a share capital of GBP 1,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares of GBP 1.00 each; no escrow deposit or bank capital certificate is required at incorporation, but the first directors must declare that any fully paid capital has been received into the company's bank account before commencement of business.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscription made in the Memorandum shall be accepted and the subscriber shall be allotted 1,000 Ordinary Shares of GBP 1.00 each par value, fully paid; share certificates shall be issued. (2) The registered office shall be situated at the office of the registered agent in Gibraltar from the date of incorporation until otherwise resolved. (3) [Name A] is appointed first Director and [Name B] is appointed Company Secretary, each having consented, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute the incorporation filings, and engage legal counsel. (4) The Directors are authorised to obtain business, environmental, and waste-licences required for the scrap copper wire trading business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, GFSC (online index search and name confirmation; no separate reservation certificate is issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Gibraltar-licensed registered agent to check the proposed name, which must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.', against the Companies Index. Submit the name-availability request electronically via the GFSC portal or through the agent; the Registry confirms uniqueness within one to two working days. The confirmed name is held for 90 days pending incorporation. If the name is cleared, proceed immediately to drafting the constitutional documents using the exact cleared name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to three alternatives)
Registered agent engagement and KYC acceptance letter
Declaration of lawful commercial purpose (wholesale of recycled non-ferrous scrap)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or misleading, file an alternative name or request written reasons from the Registrar; a refused applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for review under Companies Act 2014 s. 8. Re-filing a revised name is the standard expedient cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Signing and Notarisation of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar notary public and licensed corporate service provider; documents are later received at the GFSC Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) comprising the company name, subscriber details, objects clause, share capital (typically GBP 1,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares), registered office clause, and articles allocating director powers. The subscriber(s) execute the M&A before a Gibraltar notary; where execution occurs overseas, signatures must be notarised and apostilled under the Hague Convention. The registered agent then collates the notarially certified counterparts and consents for filing.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association (two counterparts)
Notarised passport and proof of address of each subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner
Consent to Act of the proposed first director and company secretary
Registered office consent from the Gibraltar registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries a drafting defect under Companies Act 2014 ss. 15–25, amend the M&A and re-present the corrected pages for notarisation; no formal appeal lies against a drafting query, and the sole remedy is swift resubmission through the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Fee Payment at the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, GFSC — physical counter at Europort or GFSC e-Filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 'Application for Registration of a Private Company Limited by Shares' together with the notarised M&A, executed Consent to Act forms, and Form 3 registered-office consent. Pay the official state filing fee (GBP 86.70, approximately USD 110) by bank transfer, payment card, or GFSC deposit account. Upon verification, the Registrar issues Form 2 'Certificate of Incorporation'. Expedited same-day incorporation is available where the complete package is lodged before 11:00 and the expedited fee is paid.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Registration (signed)
Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to Act (director and company secretary)
Form 3 Registered Office Consent
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, the Registry issues a Notice of Deficiency; correct and re-file within 21 days to preserve the original priority date. A refusal of registration may be appealed to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, and pre-incorporation contracts remain at the applicant's risk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Allotment and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors convened by the registered agent at the Gibraltar registered office; GFSC Companies Registry receives statutory notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the pro-forma First Board Resolution: adopt the M&A, confirm the registered office, allot the subscriber shares, appoint the first director and company secretary (both mandatory under Gibraltar law), authorise opening of corporate bank accounts, and approve issuance of share certificates. Maintain the Register of Members, Register of Directors and Secretaries, and minute book at the registered office; file any required notices of directors with the Registry.
required_dossiers: Executed First Board Resolution
Register of Members (members ledger)
Register of Directors and Secretaries
Consent to Act records
Share certificates issued to the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain statutory registers or notify director changes is a criminal offence under Companies Act 2014; timely remedy consists of filing late notifications under s. 688 and applying to the Registrar for penalty remission where the default arose through inadvertence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence, Fire Clearance and Waste/Environmental Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Licensing Office (HM Government of Gibraltar); Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change; Civil Protection and Fire Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the Business Licence application under the Business Licensing Act 2020 for 'Wholesale of Waste and Scrap — Recyclable Non-Ferrous Metals', attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, premises plan, fire certificate, and environmental screening request. For cross-border movement of shredded copper scrap, file the Transfrontier Shipment of Waste prior-written-notification (Form A) with the Department of the Environment and obtain a waste dealer's permit. Physical operations, storage, weighbridge use, and consignment may commence only after all licences and permits are granted.
required_dossiers: Business Licence application form and annual fee
Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles
Fire and health-and-safety clearance from Civil Defence
Site layout, drainage and weighbridge plan
EIA screening opinion application
Transfrontier waste shipment notification (Form A)
Contract with a Gibraltar-licensed waste transporter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A licence refusal may be appealed to the Business Licensing Appeals Tribunal within 21 days; environmental objections are curable by submitting a waste management and mitigation plan; operation before clearance is prohibited and may attract enforcement action, so interim corrective submissions are the primary remedy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry, HM Government of Gibraltar (Business Licensing Act 2020)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence for 'Wholesale of Waste and Scrap — Recyclable Non-Ferrous Metals'; Transfrontier Shipment of Waste Consent; Waste Dealer Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier B — Screening Opinion / Initial Environmental Evaluation. A full EIA Report is triggered if the facility stores or processes more than 10,000 tonnes of scrap per annum or is sited within 200 metres of residential areas or NATURA 2000 protected sites (Gibraltar Harbour and North Front).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no direct discharge to groundwater or storm drains; wash water must be recycled or discharged to foul sewer after treatment to suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L and pH 6–9. Fugitive dust (PM10) must not exceed 50 µg/m³ at the site boundary; noise limited to 65 dB(A) daytime at the nearest sensitive receptor; any oil, coolant, or PVC insulation residues must be segregated and managed as hazardous waste under the Gibraltar Waste Management Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Protection and Fire Services covering emergency access, extinguisher coverage, and hazard zoning between copper fines and PVC insulation waste; structural load approval for the weighbridge pad and container stacking certified by a Gibraltar chartered engineer; Occupational Health and Safety clearance including PPE, permit-to-work for shredding/cutting, and workplace dust-exposure monitoring plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax) for direct taxes; HM Customs of Gibraltar for indirect/customs taxes. Filing portals: Gibraltar Online Services System (GOSS) and Customs Declaration Service (CDS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company is a foreign legal person; it is not automatically registered in Gibraltar. If it acquires Gibraltar tax nexus (central management and control, permanent establishment, or Gibraltar-source income), it must file Form TN-1 with the Commissioner of Income Tax within 21 days to obtain a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN), and must appoint a fiscal agent resident in Gibraltar if it cannot be represented. For cross-border goods movements, it must apply separately to HM Customs for a Gibraltar EORI number (GI prefix) through CDS before filing any export/import declaration. Because Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area, no VAT registration ID is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The company may elect under section 50 of the Cayman Companies Act for a 20-year Tax Exemption Certificate, preserving its tax-exempt-zone status. For Gibraltar direct tax, the company may elect to be assessed as a non-resident company under section 6 of the Income Tax Act if central management and control is outside Gibraltar, filing Form 5 with proof of place of management. Check-the-box elections are unavailable under US Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-2(b)(8)(i), as a Cayman Exempted Company is a per se corporation; hybrid mismatch elections are not separately granted by Gibraltar law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Consumer Tax (single-stage Sales and Use Tax, not VAT/GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP 0 — no annual turnover threshold; any person importing goods into, or supplying chargeable goods/services within, Gibraltar must register for Consumer Tax with HM Customs. Purely export transactions are outside the charge and do not trigger registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing, API fiscal clearance, digital stamping or transaction-control regime is enacted. Customs and tax declarations are lodged electronically via CDS and GOSS; no real-time government pre-approval of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% rate applies where physically exported goods (including shredded recycled copper wire) are removed from Gibraltar to a destination outside the EU/Gibraltar customs union area within 3 months of despatch; the exporter must hold proof of export and the goods must not have been released for free circulation in Gibraltar. Offshore services supplied to a non-Gibraltar recipient whose direct benefit is enjoyed abroad are also zero-rated. All zero-rating claims require timely filing of a Consumer Tax return using export data from CDS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Cayman Exempted Company Tax Exemption Certificate (if challenged)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Customs may audit zero-rating claims up to 6 years after export. If the required export/proof-of-payment documentation is not produced on first audit demand or before repatriation of sale proceeds, the supply is reclassified as taxable in Gibraltar; Consumer Tax becomes payable at 10%, plus default interest of 1% per month and a penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded. Fraudulent zero-rating (e.g. forged bills of lading or customs declarations) is a criminal offence under the Customs Duties Act, carrying fines of up to GIP 50,000 per invoice, seizure of goods, and revocation of the exporter's customs/consumer tax registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Her Majesty's Treasury (HM Treasury) and the Bank of England for Sterling; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) for regulated banking and foreign-exchange intermediation. Gibraltar has no separate central bank, and the Government of Gibraltar issues its own currency notes under the Currency Note Act, with residual exchange-control delegation from HM Treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible into Sterling, US Dollar, Euro and other major currencies. No statutory FX licence is required for a Cayman Exempted Company operating from Gibraltar. Profit remittance to the Cayman parent is permitted without conversion hurdle, but the corporate bank will require an evidentiary source-of-funds chain and proof of beneficial ownership to satisfy Gibraltar's anti-money-laundering (AML) legislation; there is no statutory limitation on remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Gibraltar has not imposed exchange-control or export-proceeds surrender requirements since the 1979 abolition, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts may be retained in the currency of collection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow and Operational Settlement Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account with FX Module
Operational Settlement Account with SWIFT Direct Membership

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Gibraltar's Fintech Policy incorporates EU PSD2 and enables GFSC-licensed Electronic Money Institutions to open accounts for Cayman-incorporated clients. However, a non-EU/offshore digital EMI without a Gibraltar licence is prohibited from rendering payment or e-money services to Gibraltar-based entities; and for a physically-goods scrap-copper trader, most virtual banks will decline onboarding absent a consolidated physical-banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory physical-presence requirement under Gibraltar KYC rules if a robust video-identification process is used. In practice, for a Cayman Exempted Company trading in recycled scrap copper, the bank will require the principal director and ultimate beneficial owner to undergo a live video interview, and will often mandate the presence of a locally registered agent or Gibraltar Qualified Alternate Director to confirm corporate substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman offshore structure with an opaque UBO chain and no discernible economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, articles of association, full register of directors, register of members, register of beneficial owners, tax-transparency certificate, valid good-standing certificate from the Cayman Registrar, UBO declaration, and a group-structure chart evidencing the commercial cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Physical commodity trading in non-ferrous scrap with fungible goods and cross-border counterparty risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales and purchase contracts, provisional and final invoices, warehouse receipts, bills of lading, weighbridge certificates, laboratory certificates of analysis, insurance certificates, merchant-trader sanctions-screening report, and a KYC pack of the counterparty/end-smelter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated company with no previous banking relationship or financial audit history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, projected cash-flows for 24 months, historical funding audit trail, third-party credit assessment, board resolutions opening the account, CVs of all directors and the AML compliance officer, and disclosure to the GFSC of the intended trading activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential misuse of multiple foreign SPV layers for transfer-pricing or trade-based money-laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Flow-of-funds diagram, underlying commercial rationale memorandum, independent tax and legal advice on transfer-pricing and the Cayman Exempted Company's role, complete list of all bank accounts and trading partners, and a signed written confirmation of licensed trading activity and non-involvement in metal theft or regulated waste exports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the Cayman parent must be settled via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV with an appropriate BOPS/ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., Share Capital Contribution or Shareholder Loan). GBP funds clear same-day through CHAPS, EUR through TARGET2 via SEPA, and USD through Fedwire/CHIPS. The receiving Gibraltar bank will verify the debit reference against the corporate account profile and source-of-wealth documentation already on file; the board resolution and capital subscription agreement must be presented to reject any AML challenge.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement for scrap-copper purchases and smelter payments is executed through SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers, MT202 COV interbank transfers, and documentary trade instruments using MT700 Commercial Letters of Credit or MT400 Documentary Collections. Settlement is typically denominated in USD, EUR or GBP depending on the contractual invoice currency. Each disbursement must be supported by the underlying proforma invoice, packing list, certificate of analysis and transport documents to ensure trade-based AML resilience.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Outright Transactions with GFSC-licensed or investment-grade counterparties
FX Forward Contracts with tenor up to 12 months and permitted netting under ISDA/CSA documentation
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currency pairs lacking an active deliverable market
Cross-Currency Swaps (FX Swaps and Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps) for balance-sheet and capex hedging
Vanilla Currency Options with monthly/quarterly tenors and board-approved risk limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Companies Act Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (Exempted Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies and Corporate Filing Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January for the preceding calendar year; first-year filing is prorated when the Exempted Company is incorporated after 30 June and is due no later than 31 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-payment carry a 10% statutory surcharge; after six further months of non-payment, the Registrar may strike the company off the Companies Register and the company's assets vest in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Economic Substance Annual Filing and Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC), Tax Information Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each financial year; for a calendar-year entity, by no later than 31 December following the year-end, with an indication that the distribution and service centres relevant activity applies to the scrap copper wire consignment trading.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts a penalty of CI$500 to CI$10,000 per contravention; persistent default may lead to restriction notices, court-ordered penalties, or strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies House
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Delivered within 42 days after each anniversary of incorporation; for an overseas-registered company, within 42 days after the anniversary of Gibraltar registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines not exceeding £5,000 plus a daily default fine; continued non-delivery enables the Registrar to strike off and dissolve the company after six months of unresolved default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register (BOSS) Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies / Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due at the time of the Gibraltar annual return, certifying current beneficial ownership; any share-transfer-related beneficial ownership change must be reported within 15 days after the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify may be treated as a criminal offence with fines of up to £500,000; repeat non-compliance can trigger strike-off because the annual return cannot be confirmed without the UBO data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Economic Substance Annual Notification / Substance Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax, Economic Substance Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; for a 31 December year-end, by the following 31 December each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalties between £500 and £5,000 for each occasion of default; failure to file or to demonstrate substance can trigger further tax-compliant measures and international exchange of information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Audited Financial Statements Filing (where audit exemption is not available)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company, within 10 months after the accounting reference period; for a public company, within 7 months.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Gibraltar Companies Act range from £250 to £1,000 depending on the length of delay; sustained non-filing after notice is grounds for administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For this Cayman Exempted Company, mandatory independent audit is primarily activity-driven: Cayman Companies Law does not ordinarily impose an audit on a commercial exempted company doing business wholly outside Cayman, but audit becomes compulsory if the entity holds a CIMA licence or registration in a regulated sector such as banking, insurance, mutual funds, private funds, or securities dealing; in parallel, if the company is registered in Gibraltar and exceeds the Gibraltar small-company audit-exemption criteria under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, audited financial statements must be prepared and filed with the Registrar.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the default framework for a Cayman Exempted Company; Cayman also accepts US GAAP where properly applied. If Gibraltar statutory accounts are filed, they must comply with IFRS as adopted in Gibraltar / the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, or with Gibraltar GAAP for non-listed private entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered office must maintain and update the beneficial ownership register at each annual return date and reconcile it against the share register and share-transfer ledger. If any transfer of shares occurs, the statutory register must be amended before the annual confirmation; any resulting change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the Cayman beneficial ownership authorities and the Gibraltar BOSS register within 15 days. An annual confirmation return is filed simultaneously with the annual return, certifying that the UBO data are current and accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 4,200 per year for the combined Cayman and Gibraltar registered office and corporate agent services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 22,000 per year for a certified audit if required; USD 2,500 - USD 5,500 per year for an unaudited accounts compilation or independent review.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for the Cayman Exempted Company (Cayman Islands imposes no corporate income tax; the company also remains outside the Gibraltar tax net if it is not managed and controlled in Gibraltar and has no Gibraltar permanent establishment or Gibraltar-source income). Gibraltar-resident companies otherwise face a 12.5% statutory headline rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cayman Exempted Company enjoys a 20-year tax undertaking guarantee from the Cayman Islands Government under the Companies Act; no income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, payroll tax, or stamp duty. Gibraltar grants de facto exemption to non-resident exempted companies with no Gibraltar-source profits, and Gibraltar itself charges no capital gains tax and no dividend withholding tax.
